title: Help
desc: MineDeck quick start, common tasks, FAQ, data locations and known limits.
lead: New to MineDeck? Start with the quick start. Summarised from the repository README. The MineDeck interface itself is in Chinese; menu names are translated here.

steps: Open MineDeck and click New server (新建服务器).
Choose type, version and build, accept the EULA and create.
Click Start. When the console shows Done (...)! the server is up.
Players on the same network connect to this PC's LAN IP:port. For players elsewhere, add a tunnel under Tunnels (内网穿透), bind it to the server with start-with-server, and send them the public address.

items: Run a command: instance → Console → input at the bottom.
Change settings: instance → Common settings or All settings. Settings that need a restart are marked.
Memory or Java: instance → Memory / Launch.
No window: MineDeck.exe -nogui. Default port 27333, set with -port 27333; a random port is used if taken. The address and token are written to the log.
stdio bridge for local AI tools: MineDeck.exe -mcp; MineDeck must already be running.

items.q: Do I need to install Java?
items.a: No. A matching installed major version is used directly; otherwise MineDeck downloads a private runtime without changing system Java.

items.q: How do players outside my network join?
items.a: Add OpenFrp, SakuraFrp or your own frps under Tunnels, bind it to the server and enable start-with-server. Players on the same network need no tunnel.

items.q: Which versions and server types are supported?
items.a: Minecraft 1.12.2 up to the latest release in the manifest, including 26.x, across 12 server types (see Features). Modrinth .mrpack and CurseForge zips can be imported.

items.q: The server won't start. Where do I look first?
items.a: Check the error banner at the top of the console; its 13 rule types do not need AI. With AI configured you can click Analyse with AI or ask the assistant.

items.q: Will AI change my server on its own? Does it cost extra?
items.a: Your provider charges for usage; MineDeck estimates costs from public prices and supports daily budgets. Reading logs happens directly; config changes, Java switches, restarts and mod installs need a confirmation card. In-game commands are limited to authorised players and enabled templates; op and execute never run.

items.q: What do my friends need to install?
items.a: AI companion: the companion client mod matching the server version (on the Download page). Music sharing: the same Simple Voice Chat version on server and clients; MineDeck installs the bridge mod on the server.

Use stable for everyday play. The 3.1.0 betas add handover packs, the mod cart, pending modpack files, adopting existing servers and per-server Java, and may still have problems. Run a beta from its own folder, back up before trying an existing server, and note that betas do not auto-update to each other.
MineDeck.exe is not code-signed, so SmartScreen may block the first run. Click More info → Run anyway. You can verify the SHA-256 first as described on the Download page.

items.q: Friends on my LAN can't connect?
items.a: The first time a server starts, Windows Firewall may ask for permission. LAN players can connect after you allow it.

items: Everything defaults to the exe's folder: servers, backups, runtimes, cache and logs\ops.
If you delete runtimes, existing servers lose their portable Java and need it prepared again under Memory / Launch.
To uninstall, delete the exe's folder and %LocalAppData%\MineDeck.
Windows Firewall may prompt the first time a server starts.
Forge and NeoForge installers still fetch some libraries from official sources and can fail even after mirrors and retries.
On Windows 10, music sharing can only capture the whole playback device.
Paper and Purpur have no mirror in mainland China.
